situation: A guest who cannot sign in
given: the Portal sign-in page, and a guest who has forgotten their password or has no account
then: the form says, once and under the Sign in button, to ask the front desk when there is no account or the password is forgotten; it carries no link to a page that says the same (PORTAL-08); /forgot-password and /reset-password still open a page that says resetting by email is not available yet and to ask the front desk, with a way back, in the address's language, not a 404
test_name: guest-portal-ux.spec.ts: a Guest who cannot sign in is told who can help, and the reset addresses are not a 404; portal-placeholders-ux.spec.ts: the Portal sign-in answers a forgotten password where the Guest is, with no link to a page that says it again

when: it is sent empty, or refused
then: an empty form says in the page's language to enter the email and password (not the browser's own bubble) and puts focus in the first field; a refusal puts focus back in the email field; the page and its titles name where the guest is
test_name: guest-portal-ux.spec.ts: a refused or empty sign-in says so in the page's language and puts focus back in the form

given: a Portal address with no language, such as / or /stay
then: it opens in the language last chosen, else the first the browser asks for that the Portal speaks, else Turkish; reading an address with a language remembers it
test_name: guest-portal-ux.spec.ts: a link with no language opens in the one the browser asked for, then in the one last chosen

given: an address under a language that is not a page
then: the Portal's own page answers 404 in that language, drawn in the same frame as sign-in (wordmark, language menu), titled with what happened, with the way back the visitor can use: Sign in when signed out, Go to my stay when signed in (PORTAL-06); a runtime failure shows a sentence and Try again, not the framework's bare page
test_name: guest-portal-ux.spec.ts: a missing page is the Portal's own, in the language of the address; portal-placeholders-ux.spec.ts: an address that is no page is drawn in the Portal's frame, titled, and leads the visitor where they can go; portal-placeholders-ux.spec.ts: a signed-in Guest on an address that is no page is led back to their stay

given: a guest with an in-house stay and a later booking
then: the stay they are in comes first and the booking after it is set apart; the type reads Stay type: Resident or Guest; the status reads Staying now; an open end reads No end date
test_name: guest-portal-ux.spec.ts: a Guest sees the stay they are in first, read in plain words, and a finished one is not called unset-up

given: a guest whose stays are all departed or cancelled
then: the page says You have no current stay and to contact the property if they expected one, and never that the property has not set up their stay (the answer is the same as for every other reason there is no current stay, ADR 0009)
test_name: guest-portal-ux.spec.ts: a Guest sees the stay they are in first, read in plain words, and a finished one is not called unset-up

then: deferred, an owner's decision: showing a read-only departed or cancelled stay changes what ADR 0009 deliberately keeps indistinguishable (a departed guest, a staff member and a property without the capability see the same empty answer); the query stays reserved and in house until the owner decides (GP-02)

given: a guest who has a stay
then: deferred: nothing writes stays.user_id, so most stays have no Portal; accounts are created by hand until an invitation flow exists (ADR 0009); the sign-in page says to ask the front desk

given: a guest who forgot their password
then: deferred: there is no email delivery (blueprint 5.12); the sign-in and help pages name the front desk instead, and the page can gain a form when mail exists

given: a runtime failure in the Portal
then: deferred: neither application has a client error reporter; the Portal's error page logs the failure's digest to the console, as its sign-in form does, until one exists

situation: The sign-in gate is a landmark
given: the sign-in page of the Portal or the workspace
when: a screen reader lists the page's landmarks
then: the page has one main, holding the heading and the form, and one banner holding the wordmark and the language switch (GP-10)

situation: Changing language on the help page
given: /forgot-password or /reset-password?token=…, a guest opening the language menu
then: they stay on the same route with the same query, so a token survives the change (PORTAL-07); the 404 page's menu leads to sign-in or the stay, the pages it can offer
test_name: portal-placeholders-ux.spec.ts: changing language on the help page keeps the page and what its address carries

situation: Touch targets on the Portal's first screens
given: a phone-width window, with a mouse or a finger
when: the language menu is open, or the 404 page is shown
then: every language in the menu and the page's button are at least 44 px tall (PORTAL-05)
test_name: portal-placeholders-ux.spec.ts: at a phone's width every language in the menu is a touch target, even under a mouse; portal-placeholders-ux.spec.ts: an address that is no page is drawn in the Portal's frame, titled, and leads the visitor where they can go

given: a signed-in Guest whose account has a name, has none, or has their address as the name
when: they look at the account in the rail or the bar
then: the name on the account leads with the address beneath it; with no name, the part of the address before the @ leads; an address is never printed twice as both name and address (PORTAL-09). The Stay holds no name to read instead, and a Resident reaches no Guest record (ADR 0009)
test_name: portal-placeholders-ux.spec.ts: the Guest's corner names them, not their address
